top_choice_rationale: P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) rests on a clear new principle: a designed bifunctional molecule forms a measurable, cooperative ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase, so the protein is eliminated rather than occupied. It is a new capability reproduced across many laboratories, and the citation can rest on the chemical principle and design rules without claiming clinical success. The omission of Sakamoto, Kim and the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) is real and must be stated openly, but the narrower PROTAC-focused citation is defensible. P002 (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a mature, cleanly attributed method, but it is an extension of the field recognised in 2010, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I share a Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, which is ordinary colleague contact, and none of the credited laureates in P001 or P002 is a known collaborator or colleague.
